T: Hedge, grown wild and high. Somebody was told to stop gardening.
v: The hedge has grown right across the path here, thick as a wall.
Someone who knows the wild could find a way through.
L: The old law, carved in stone. The letters are old; you can't make them out.
R: Beyond the law stone, a sealed little garden. One white rose grows here.
Beside it, a stone head, a king's, set carefully so it faces the rose.
>: The way back out to the town.

objects.name: Hugo Thornbeard
lines: Mind the hedges. They've got feelings. Well. Forty personalities, anyway.

answer: At the heart. Past the overgrowth. The king ordered the maze left wild so nobody'd read it.
A gardener notices when he's told to stop gardening.
The little prince used to hide in here instead of drilling. Big hands. Small courage. Lovely lad.

questions.ask: Who put the head by the rose?
answer: …I found it in the Kaloseum's drain, thirty years back. Seemed wrong to leave a king looking at a drain.

questions.ask: Some gardener. This place is a mess.
answer: Shh. Not in front of the hedges.
* Somewhere to your left, a hedge rustles in a hurt sort of way.
That was Philippa. She's sensitive. Now look what you've done.

lines: At the end of a path that goes nowhere, where a boy once hid from his lessons: a Heart Piece.
